Using your own modem with TPG

Check your modem is compatible

You’ll need to verify that your modem is compatible with TPG at your address. TPG will only be able to provide general support on your service – and you’ll need to contact the modem manufacturer directly for any technical support needed.

Understand your tech type

If you have FTTN, FTTB or FTTC at your address, your BYO modem will need to be VDSL2 compatible. Make sure you check your modem device guide to see if your modem supports PPPoE and is VDSL2 compatible.

Consider a TPG modem for streamlined support

If you use a TPG-supplied modem and need support, our team is available to help. In many cases, we’ll be able to connect to your modem remotely and help troubleshoot your service.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I get nbn® at my address?

To see if you can get nbn® at your home, check your address.

If you can’t currently get nbn® at your address, you may be eligible for a Home Wireless or 5G Home Internet plan.

Do I have to switch to nbn®?

If you live in an area where nbn® has been rolled out and you want to keep your landline or internet service, you need to switch to nbn® before the copper-based services in your area are disabled. This may occur about 18 months after nbn® becomes available in your area.

You don’t need to switch to nbn® if you live in an area where nbn® Fixed Wireless is available. Copper-based services will not be disabled in Fixed Wireless areas, however we recommend switching and enjoy the speeds of nbn®.

What are the different nbn® connection types?

TPG delivers the following nbn® connection types, depending on your location:

    • Fibre to the Premises (FTTP): fibre-optic cable from a fibre node directly to the premises, e.g., house or business.

    • Fibre to the Node (FTTN): fibre-optic cable to a neighbourhood node, and from there, using the existing copper network to the premises.

    • Fibre to the Building (FTTB): fibre-optic cable to the basement of multi-dwelling units such as apartment blocks and from there using the existing copper wire to the premises.

    • Fibre to the Curb (FTTC): fibre-optic cable to an outdoor pit near the premises and from there using the existing copper network to the premises.

    • Cable/Hybrid Fibre Coaxial (HFC): a combination of fibre and coaxial cable.

    • Fixed Wireless: radio communications from an nbn® Fixed Wireless facility directly to a small outdoor antenna attached to your premises.

What modem is included?

You may choose to bring your own compatible modem or have a high-speed Wi-Fi 7 modem supplied by us:

  • $0 modem if you stay connected for 24 months
  • $200 fee if you cancel early or return the modem at no cost

High-speed Wi-Fi 7 modem:

  • Powered by the latest Wi-Fi 7 technology. Compatible devices required.
  • Smarter Wi-Fi that adapts
  • Plug and play setup
  • Made for super-fast plans
  • Optional mobile backup (mobile data and compatible device required).

Delivery fee of $10 applies.

Where you purchase equipment from TPG as a consumer within the meaning of the Competition and Consumer Act, 2010, that Act creates certain warranties which will apply in respect of the equipment.

What is the process for nbn® installation?

Have you already begun the installation process? Track your installation progress.

How long does installation take?

Installation of an nbn® service generally takes less than 10 business days but can take longer in some cases. This depends on the demand of nbn® services in your area and the availability of a technician to perform the installation.

  1. Schedule an appointment

    If your premises had an active nbn® service connected previously, then you likely won’t require a technician’s visit.

    If installation is required, TPG will organise the appointment for you. You or an authorised person over 18 years of age will need to be at the premises on the day of the technician visit.

  2. Before your installation appointment

    Identify where you want the nbn® equipment to be installed. The ideal area is:

        • close to an accessible power point;
        • cool, dry and ventilated; and
        • away from busy areas where the equipment may be knocked and damaged.

    The installer will confirm whether the requested work can be performed without additional charges.

  3. What to expect during installation

    If your building doesn’t already have a fibre-optic cable connected, running the cable into your premises may require digging a small trench, or, if it’s coming from overhead, some minor clearing of vegetation. nbn® has a strict "leave it as it's found" policy so there won’t be any damage to your property.

    Furniture may need to be moved and some drilling work might be required to mount the equipment, so be prepared for noise and dust. Some locations might not be possible due to safety or other considerations such as if there is additional wiring work required.

    If your premises already have fibre-optic cable connected to a Premises Connection Device (PCD), standard installations normally take 2–4 hours.

    If your premises don’t have the fibre optic cable connected, a standard installation could take 4–8 hours. If you request a non-standard installation, the time required may be longer.

  4. What nbn® equipment will be installed?

    If you select the modem, TPG will provide you with a high-speed Wi-Fi 7 modem with VoIP capabilities that will let you connect to the internet and make/receive phone calls using your TPG Voice Service.

    Your nbn® installer will physically connect the FTTC connection to the nbn® network and install the NBN® Connection Device (NCD) in your premises.

This may include:

    • NBN® Utility Box or Premises Connection Device (PCD) 
    • NBN® Connection Box or Network Termination Device (NTD) 

Is there a modem backup option if I’m experiencing connection issues?

If you run into connection issues over your fixed line, you can configure the TPG Wi-Fi Max modem to connect to a mobile hotspot network from your mobile phone and automatically use your mobile data. To find out how to configure your modem, head to our support hub and we’ll help you get set up.

Keep in mind : the mobile backup feature will use your mobile data at your own cost.

How do I switch to TPG nbn®?

    1. Check what plans you’re eligible for and sign up on our nbn® page.

    2. Wait for your new service to be activated (this typically takes less than 10 business days)

    3. After your new service has been activated, contact your current provider to have these services cancelled, to ensure you don’t receive any further bills

TPG recommends you check with your current phone and/or internet service provider regarding contractual commitments and termination or disconnection fees associated with your current services. TPG is not responsible for these charges.

Note: If you are also porting your existing number to TPG, don’t cancel your phone service until the number has been ported.

Am I eligible for an nbn® Fibre Upgrade?

Enter your address on our nbn® page and select a Fibre Upgrade plan if you’re eligible. You’ll either stay on your current TPG nbn® plan or be connected to an interim plan while nbn® completes the installation. Learn more about nbn® Fibre Upgrade.

Do I need a new modem for my fibre upgrade?

Our fibre upgrade plans require a compatible modem. You can find our compatible modem requirements here. Devices that don’t support Wi-Fi 6 and Gigabit Ethernet may not be able to achieve the speeds available on our high-speed nbn® plans with maximum speeds higher than 100Mbps.

I live at a rental property, can I still upgrade to nbn® Fibre?

You’ll need the landlord’s permission to upgrade to nbn® Fibre at their premises as it may require work to the property to set up the connection, such as drilling into walls.

We’ve created a customisable letter that you can send to your landlord or property manager. Download the letter template.

Once you have approval, we can proceed with the upgrade.

What if I’m moving homes?

Your plan is specific to your current address and your new address may be eligible for different plans. Check your new address to see what plans you can get.

There are no fees for moving your plan to a new home, but an additional once off $300 nbn® New Development Charge may apply if you are moving and the premises you are moving to is identified by nbn® as being within the site boundary of a new development.

How do payments work?

All TPG services are prepaid. You must pay the monthly recurring charges in advance. You have the option to make additional prepayment for usage that is not within the included value (if any) for the plan that you have acquired. If there are insufficient funds in your prepaid balance, you will not be able to make any usage that is not part of your included value. Prepayments can be made during registration or after activation via your online account. If you choose to make additional prepayment, the amount will be debited from your nominated bank account or credit card. If you do not use the prepayment, it will be forfeited to us when you cancel the service. You agree that no bill will be provided for this service and that direct debiting of your account or charge to your credit card may occur notwithstanding that no bill is provided and that it may occur even though you may not have had the opportunity to check charges at least 10 working days before the debit. We will send you messages about your usage during the month.

TPG Voice Services

What is TPG Voice Service?

TPG Voice Service on NBN FTTN, FTTB, FTTC, Cable (HFC) and Fixed Wireless is a Digital Voice Service which is delivered using Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) technology. Digital Voice Service requires a broadband connection and power to the Wi-Fi modem router supplied by TPG. If there is a broadband connection outage in your premises due to power or other faults, the Digital Voice Service will not work, and you cannot make phone calls including "000" emergency calls.

Once an nbn® Bundle plan is purchased, you cannot separately cancel nbn® Broadband or Voice Service. Cancellation will cease both services. You cannot purchase Voice Service as a standalone service.

What does TPG Voice Service support?

TPG Voice Service supports: fax to national numbers in the Telstra, Optus, AAPT and Primus PSTN network.

TPG Voice Service doesn’t support:

    • fax to international numbers;

    • Priority Assistance Scheme;

    • analogue modems;

    • calls to 19/1900, 0500 numbers and Universal International Freephone Numbers (UIFN); or

    • old dial-up technology devices with built in modems, such as EFTPOS, Back-to-Base Alarms and Foxtel Program purchases. These devices have been replaced by Internet Protocol (IP) enabled devices. For further details on IP-enabled devices contact your device supplier.

Can I port my number to TPG?

You can port (transfer) your phone number from Telstra, Optus, AAPT, Primus or Powertel to TPG. We may not be able to port your number in some circumstances, including where you fail to provide correct account details, or as a result of contractual obligations with your existing provider.

TPG can also supply a new number, which will be allocated based on your registered address. TPG will supply the Integrated Public Number Database (IPND) with your address details for emergency services (000) calling.

If you are porting your number to TPG, you can still make outbound calls but inbound calling to your number will not commence until porting is complete, which will take 1–5 business days.

Will my phone service work in a power outage?

TPG nbn® services on FTTN, FTTB, FTTC, HFC and Fixed Wireless technologies will NOT work in the event of a power outage. The Voice Service requires a broadband connection and power to the Wi-Fi modem supplied by TPG. If there is a broadband connection outage in your premises due to power or other faults, the Digital Voice Service will not work and you cannot make phone calls including "000" emergency calls.

Do I need a backup power service?

nbn® services require a backup battery unit to keep power going to your nbn® Network Termination Device in the event of a power outage, so that some elements of your telephone service can continue to operate for about 5 hours during the power outage.

TPG nbn® service does not include the supply of a backup battery unit. This means during a power outage, you will not be able to make or receive any calls, including calls to emergency services. Please ensure that you have an alternative method to make calls such as a mobile phone.

What Call Packs are available?

Pay As You Go: 

Charges for calls not included in your service will be charged on a Pay As You Go basis. These charges will be deducted from your prepayment. For information on the Pay As You Go rates, check out our call rates. There are some calls that are not supported such as calls to 19/1900. For more information, check out here.

Oz Talk Call Pack: 

This call pack allows you to make unlimited Local Calls (excluding 13/1300 numbers and calls to Directory Assistance (1223)), unlimited Standard National Calls to Landlines and unlimited National Calls to Mobiles. There are some calls that are not supported such as calls to 19/1900. For more information, check out here. Charges for calls made that are not included in the call pack (e.g. calls to 13/1300, International Calls and Directory Services (1223)) will be charged at listed TPG rates by deducting usage charges from your prepaid balance. The service is for residential consumers only and may not be used for commercial purposes.

Big Talk Call Pack: 

This call pack allows you to make unlimited Local Calls (excluding 13/1300 numbers and calls to Directory Assistance (1223)), unlimited Standard National Calls to Landlines, unlimited National Calls to Mobiles and 100 minutes each month to call any Landline and Mobile in any destination (satellite phones excluded) listed in the Big Talk Call Pack on our International Call Rates page. Standard per minute rates listed on our International Call Rates page apply after the first 100 minutes of International Calls each month and for calls to satellite phones. Unused included international minutes expire at the end of each month. There are some calls that are not supported such as calls to 19/1900. For more information, check out here. Charges for calls made that are not included in the call pack (e.g. calls to 13/1300, and Directory Services (1223)) will be charged at listed TPG rates by deducting usage charges from your prepaid balance. The service is for residential consumers only and may not be used for commercial purposes.

Extra Talk Call Pack: 

This call pack allows you to make unlimited Local Calls (excluding 13/1300 numbers and calls to Directory Assistance (1223)), unlimited Standard National Calls to Landlines, unlimited National Calls to Mobiles and unlimited calls to Landline and Mobile numbers to the following 23 destinations (excluding satellite phones): Canada, China, France, Germany, Greece, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Malaysia, Netherlands, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, Korea (South), Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, United Kingdom and United States. Standard per minute rates listed on our International Call Rates page apply for International Calls to other destinations and calls to satellite phones. Charges for calls made that are not included in the call pack (e.g. calls to 13/1300, Directory Services (1223) and satellite phones) will be charged at listed TPG rates by deducting usage charges from your prepaid balance. There are some calls that are not supported such as calls to 19/1900. For more information, check out here. The service is for residential consumers only and may not be used for commercial purposes.

Can I use TPG Voice for local calls only and choose another provider for other calls (national long distance, international, calls to mobiles)?

No. TPG Voice is full service including line rental, local, national, international and home to mobile calls. Customers must not preselect to another carrier or use the TPG Voice service to make override calls on a third-party network.

How do I list my TPG Voice Service number in the directory?

  5. Click 'Update' at the bottom of the page

Porting your phone number to TPG Voice

We’ll check if it’s possible to port your phone number to TPG as part of your nbn order. You’ll need to give us your Account Number with your current phone provider – you can find this on your bill for the phone service.

We can usually port phone numbers from Telstra, Optus, AAPT, Primus and Powertel but there may be some exceptions depending on your service contract.

How number porting works

  1. Once your nbn is connected, your TPG Voice service will be set up with a temporary phone number that you can use to make calls.
  2. It’ll take another 1 to 5 business days to finish porting your phone number to TPG Voice. Incoming calls won’t work during this time.
  3. Once the port is done, you can make and receive calls using your phone number.
    Important: Do not cancel your phone service with your old provider until your phone number is working with TPG Voice, or the port may fail.

Checking TPG Voice usage and managing your spend

Reverse Charge Calls/Collect Calls can’t be received by a TPG Voice service.

You can also use Call Barring to prevent certain types of calls from being made.

Will my TPG Voice number be supplied to emergency services?

We’ll provide your TPG Voice phone number and address details to the Integrated Public Number Database (IPND) for the purpose of 000 emergency calls.

Are there any fees for installing, changing or cancelling my plan?

New development charge 

The nbn® New Development Charge of $300 applies if your premises is identified by nbn® as being within the site boundary of a new development. 
 

Missed or changed appointment fee 

If you give TPG less than 3 working days’ notice of any change in appointment, a $109 fee applies. 
 

Changing my plan at the same address 

There is no change fee if you want to upgrade or downgrade your plan at the same address.  

Note: TPG nbn® customers are not able to change their plan to a TPG ADSL2+/ADSL services. 
 

Cancelling my plan 

There are no cancellation fees for no lock-in contracts. However, you may be required to pay for the Modem if you leave prior to 24 months (refer to Total Minimum Charge under the Plans table above). The modem fee is $200. Alternatively, you may choose to return your Modem in Good Working Order within 21 days to avoid paying the modem fee. ‘Good Working Order’ means the returned Modem is near new with only minor signs of wear and tear, and includes all original equipment. Cancelling the nbn® service will also cancel any other TPG products that are only available with nbn®. Should those products have their own contract, you are liable for their associated break fees. If your order is withdrawn after receiving the Modem we supplied to you, then you will need to return the Modem to us in Good Working Order within 21 days of cancellation/withdrawal. If you do not return the Modem, then you will be charged a Modem non-return fee of $200.

If you are inside the minimum contract term for an nbn® bundle, there may be an early termination fee. Check your plan’s Critical Information Summary for the exact fee. 
 

Incorrect nbn® fault lodged 

Lodged nbn® fault is considered incorrect if NBN Co finds no fault or the fault is caused by your equipment.

To redeem the Offer, the lower price must be (1) available to the general public; (2) offered on the same or an equivalent NBN plan as the TPG Eligible Plan chosen to price beat (‘Your Service’); (3) advertised on an Eligible Provider's publicly available website at the time of purchasing Your Service, or within 7 days of purchase if you submit the online claim form. Eligible Provider’s NBN plan must be available (or have been available within the 7 day period) for immediate purchase using the same payment method. Customer may be asked to provide evidence in support of a price beat guarantee claim, including the date, price and terms and conditions of an Eligible Provider’s offer.

The Offer means that the total cost of the plan fees for Your Service for the first 12 months will be lower than an Eligible Provider’s total advertised retail plan fees for the first 12 months (‘Provider’s Offer’). It does not mean that your plan fees will necessarily be lower than the Eligible Provider's offer during the first month or any particular month of Your Service. Once your price beat guarantee claim is verified, we will create an offer for Your Service at the lower price for the first 12 months. The Offer applies only to the plan fees for an Eligible Provider's plan and Your Service and does not include the cost of any installation, modem or other add-ons or inclusions. After the first 12 months, your monthly plan fees will be charged at the then undiscounted monthly price for Your Service.

Standard upfront undiscounted payment applies on sign up to Your Service. Offer will be applied to subsequent bills (as applicable) as an adjustment or credit. Offer can only be claimed once per Eligible Plan and is only available at point of sale or, if you submit the online claim form, within 7 days of the date of sign up of Your Service. Offer is not available if any of the eligibility criteria is not met, or we determine the evidence you provide to be fake or falsified in any way.

The Eligible Provider's Offer is ineligible for this Offer if it is: part of a bundle with any other product or service (for example, mobile, banking, utility, etc.); inclusive of a locked in contract; inclusive of non-price incentives (including but not limited to cashback, coupon offers or gift cards, reward points, speed upgrade); for commercial / business NBN service; a corporate benefit price; priced incorrectly.

This offer is available in conjunction with other in-market offers, however such other offer (as applicable) will be taken into account when calculating the total cost of the plan fees for Your Service for the first 12 months. Excludes customers changing the rate or plan of their existing plan. Offer is forfeited if you cancel or change your plan or location within the first 12 months. Offer: Bundling discount

$5 off monthly plan fees with a linked TPG internet plan from month 7, for new and existing TPG customers who link their eligible mobile plan with an eligible internet plan. Eligible mobile plans: Medium 50GB and Large 100GB TPG SIM Only Mobile plans. Eligible internet plans: NBN, Home Wireless Broadband, 5G Home Broadband, FTTB and FTTH plans. Other offers: Cannot be used in conjunction with any other offers. If any other offers or discounts apply on your eligible mobile plan, bundling discount will be paused until the end of that offer duration period. Linking plans: Linked accounts are shown in My Account. If either of your eligible mobile plan or eligible internet plan are not shown, please call Customer Support on 13 14 23 to link accounts. Bundling discount applies from the next invoice after your eligible plans have been linked. If your eligible internet plan is cancelled, becomes inactive or is unlinked from your eligible mobile plan, bundling discount is forfeited from your next invoice. Personal use: Offer not for commercial, resale or transfer purposes, or exchangeable or redeemable for cash. Available until withdrawn. Offer subject to change.
